text: The third season of the American reality competition streaming series The Circle began on Netflix on September 8, 2021, and concluded on September 29, 2021. The season was announced in March 2020 when Netflix renewed The Circle for a second and third season, with Michelle Buteau returning as host. Like previous seasons, players compete to become the most popular without meeting face-to-face; instead, they communicate through a specially designed app where they can portray themselves in any way they choose, including catfishing. The contestants live in separate apartments within the same building and rate one another from first to last place. At the end of each rating period, their average ratings are revealed from lowest to highest, with the two highest-rated players typically becoming "Influencers" and the rest at risk of being "blocked" by them. Occasionally, the blocking process includes twists such as instantly blocking the lowest-rated players, keeping the Influencers' identities secret, or blocking multiple players at once. Blocked players are eliminated but are given the chance to meet one remaining player in person, with a video message shown the next day to reveal if they were real or fake. The season finale features a final rating, with the highest-rated player winning the US$100,000 prize, and fans voting for their favorite player, who wins the Fan Favorite award and US$10,000. James Andre Jefferson Jr. won the season by playing as himself and receiving the US$100,000 prize, while Matthew Pappadia as "Ashley" was the runner-up. Keisha "Kai" Ghost won the Fan Favorite award and US$10,000. The first eight players—Matt, Calvin, Nick, Kai, Ruksana, Michelle, Daniel, Ava, and Chanel—enter the apartment building and create their profiles. Initially, Calvin and Kai place in the top two, but The Circle reveals Kai is the sole influencer, who decides to block Ava and Chanel. Ava and Chanel choose to clone Michelle, re-entering as "Blue Michelle" and leaving the original Michelle as "Orange Michelle." The players have one day to decide which Michelle to keep. Orange Michelle is blocked unanimously and visits Blue Michelle before leaving. Later, two new players, "Isabella" and "Jackson," enter and are able to talk to each other before meeting the rest. Isabella and Jackson settle in, with Jackson starting a private chat with Kai and flirting with her. The players rate each other from first to sixth, with new players unable to be rated. After the ratings, Kai places second and Ruksana places first; both influencers chat and decide who to block. Kai visits Michelle after deciding to block her, learning she is not the real Michelle but instead Ava and Chanel. Later, the players learn that Orange Michelle was the real Michelle and Blue Michelle was the clone, confirmed by their goodbye messages. The players rate each other from first to seventh, with Nick placing first and Daniel second; both become Influencers and choose one player to block. Daniel blocks Jackson, and Nick blocks Ruksana. "Jackson" visits Nick and reveals she is actually Rachel. Nick confides with Rachel that "Vince" is his burner profile, received as a parting gift from Calvin. Ruksana visits Daniel. The next morning, "Vince" is removed from the game before the Circle reveals it was a burner profile handled by an existing player. New player Jacki joins the game. James brings Jacki up to speed on events in The Circle. The two main alliances—James, Kai, and Daniel on one side; Nick, Ashley, and Isabella on the other—each try to bring Jacki to their side, resulting in her receiving simultaneous group chat invites and choosing James’s group. Jacki later explains the situation to Nick to clear the air. James and Nick decide to block Daniel. When Daniel is allowed to visit a player, he chooses Isabella (Sophia), who shares her story with him. After the circle votes for the yearbook, there is a circle prom where players share their plans for the prize money if they win. In 2023, Calvin Crooks and Nick Uhlenhuth competed on the first season of Perfect Match; Crooks was eliminated in Episode Two, and Uhlenhuth finished as a finalist alongside LC Chamblin. Nick Uhlenhuth also competed on the first season of Battle Camp, where he was eliminated tenth. Rachel Ward appeared on the comedy game show Game Changer, appearing as a suitor in a Bachelor-themed episode.
